profile.reading: Per Data Foundry own site, this Austin, Texas facility (Data Foundry 02, also called Texas 2) sits at 4100 Smith School Rd and totals 325,000 square feet, providing 36 MW of power. The facility is audited to SOC 2 (SSAE 18), HIPAA, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS standards. This facility (Building 2) sits on the operator's Data Ranch campus, a named 40-acre site in Austin that also hosts the separate Data Foundry 01/Texas 1 building (Building 1, at the same street address) roughly 30 to 40 meters away, tracked separately elsewhere in this registry. The 36 MW power figure cited by the operator describes power access rather than a certified critical-IT-load rating, so it is not recorded here as critical_it_mw. Data Foundry has operated in Texas for more than two decades, with its current portfolio concentrated on this Data Ranch campus (Buildings 1 and 2), a separate Austin facility (Data Foundry 00/Austin 1), and one Houston facility (Houston 2), all tracked separately elsewhere in this registry; unlike larger REIT-owned or private-equity-backed operators, Data Foundry remains an independent Texas company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's specifications are sourced solely to the operator's own published materials. No year-opened date was located for this facility in sourcing reachable this session. Smith School Road sits in southeast Austin, a submarket that has drawn data center development in part for its distance from the downtown core's flood-prone areas and its access to major highway infrastructure. The Data Ranch campus name reflects the site's prior use, a common pattern in Austin-area data center development where operators have repurposed former rural or agricultural land on the metro's expanding edge rather than building on infill sites. No further public breakdown of tenant mix or occupancy is available for this building specifically.

reading.body:
Data Foundry Texas 2 publishes 36 MW of power capacity but no other technical specifications that would determine its suitability for AI workloads, making it impossible to assess rack density or accelerator fit from public data.

The facility occupies 325,000 square feet in Austin and holds SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications. Square footage alone does not indicate AI readiness. Power density per square foot, cooling architecture, and redundancy tier are the variables that matter for compute density, and none are published. Without a power figure tied to a cooling specification, estimating how much GPU or tensor capacity this building can host would be guesswork.

Within Texas, this site ranks among the state's 133 tracked facilities but outside the 13 that publish megawatt figures. Texas as a whole reports 389 MW across those 13 named sites. Data Foundry Texas 2's 36 MW is known, but the operator's silence on thermal budget and infrastructure design leaves its actual role in AI scaling opaque. Until the operator publishes cooling capacity and redundancy class, readers should treat power-to-space efficiency as unknown.
